summary.text: Ethan Baker is the Republican nominee for Michigan's 11th District and the mayor of Troy. An attorney who owns a Troy law practice, he worked early in his career for former President Ronald Reagan's post-presidential office. He is running on a message of bipartisan tone and reducing political division.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, he was raised by a single mother in California and moved to Oakland County with his wife, Bethany, about 17 years ago; they have three children.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Southern California, a law degree from Whittier College School of Law, a Master of Public Affairs from the University of Michigan's Ford School of Public Policy, and a certificate for senior executives in state and local government from Harvard's Kennedy School.
Began as an intern in the post-presidential office of Ronald and Nancy Reagan at age 20 and was then hired, serving more than four years as special assistant, according to his campaign website.
Practices law and owns a law practice in Troy focused on elder law, estate planning, business law and real estate.

Ran unsuccessfully in the 2014 Republican primary for Michigan State Senate District 13 (6.4% of the vote) and the 2018 Republican primary for Michigan House District 41 (44.1% to Doug Tietz's 47.7%).
Elected to the Troy City Council in 2015 and mayor of Troy in 2019; his campaign website says he was re-elected unchallenged and has served as mayor for seven years.
Chairs the Great Lakes Fishery Commission and serves as a U.S. Commissioner; his campaign website describes work restoring U.S.-Canada cooperation on Great Lakes stewardship.

Other civic roles include vice chair of Troy's Downtown Development Authority, chair of the Global Troy Advisory Committee, service on the Local Development Finance Authority, and a seat on the U.S. Conference of Mayors advisory board.
Won the Republican primary for Michigan's 11th District on August 4, 2026.
